description: With TTLCache(maxsize=2, ttl=2, timer=t), store a key at t=0. At t=2 the key is reported as gone by membership and iteration — 1 in cache is False and set(cache) does not contain it — yet len(cache) still counts it and cache.currsize still includes its size, and calling cache.expire() at t=2 returns an empty list. The entry is only cleaned up at t=3, one tick after its TTL ended. All views of the cache should agree on when an item expires.

diff --git a/tests/test_repopilot_cachetools_001.py b/tests/test_repopilot_cachetools_001.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..4d11839
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_repopilot_cachetools_001.py
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+from cachetools import TTLCache
+
+
+class Clock:
+    def __init__(self, now=10.0):
+        self.now = now
+
+    def __call__(self):
+        return self.now
+
+
+def test_expire_evicts_items_whose_ttl_ends_exactly_now():
+    clock = Clock()
+    cache = TTLCache(maxsize=10, ttl=5, timer=clock)
+    cache["a"] = 1
+    cache["b"] = 2
+    clock.now = 15.0  # both items expire at t=15
+    assert sorted(cache.expire()) == [("a", 1), ("b", 2)]
+    assert cache.currsize == 0
+    assert list(cache) == []
+
+
+def test_len_and_membership_agree_at_the_ttl_boundary():
+    clock = Clock()
+    cache = TTLCache(maxsize=10, ttl=3, timer=clock)
+    cache["k"] = "v"
+    clock.now = 13.0
+    assert "k" not in cache
+    assert len(cache) == 0
+    assert cache.get("k") is None
